extracted.intended_audience: Prospective offerors/respondents to ONR BAA N00014-22-S-B001 (academia, industry, research organizations, small businesses, UARCs, teams)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation standards for submitting white papers and full proposals to the Office of Naval Research Long Range BAA (N00014-22-S-B001), including eligibility, formatting, required content, evaluation criteria, and administrative/legal requirements. Targets proposals to be considered for contracts, grants, cooperative agreements, TIAs, or OTAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible Applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: All responsible sources from academia, industry and the research community worldwide may submit proposals under this BAA. Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs) and Minority Institutions (MIs) are encouraged. Federally Funded Research & Development Centers (FFRDCs) and Navy laboratories, military universities and warfare centers, and other DoD and civilian agency laboratories are not eligible to receive awards under this BAA (teaming with eligible principal offerors is allowed where permitted). University Affiliated Research Centers (UARCs) are eligible unless precluded by their DoD UARC contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams are encouraged; offerors must be willing to cooperate and exchange software, data and other information in integrated programs. Disclosures of current and pending support may render an applicant ineligible and must be updated prior to award and during performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracted Fundamental Research — definition and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR will follow the Under Secretary of Defense (AT&L) memorandum definition of 'contracted fundamental research' (includes RDT&E Budget Activity 1 basic research and certain Budget Activity 2 applied research performed on campus at a university). Research funded by Budget Activity 2 not performed on campus, Budget Activity 3, or Budget Activity 4 generally does not meet the definition and may be non-fundamental.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ONR will place no restriction on conduct or reporting of unclassified contracted fundamental research except as required by statute/regulation/executive order. Non-fundamental research may require restrictions and DoD pre-publication review. Prime contractors must identify and document any subcontracted work that they assert is fundamental research and confirm scoping and negotiation. Potential offerors should consult ONR Technical POCs to determine fundamental vs non-fundamental status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument Types and associated cost/share rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards may take the form of contracts, grants, cooperative agreements, Technology Investment Agreements (TIAs), and Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs) for research or prototypes, as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants: transfer of value to carry out public purpose; no fee/profit and no substantial involvement expected. Cooperative agreements: like grants but substantial Government involvement expected; no fee/profit. TIAs: assistance instrument (32 CFR Part 37) often tailored for commercial firms; to maximum extent practicable provide 50/50 cost share; no fee/profit. OTA for research: may be used for basic/applied/advanced research; to maximum extent practicable provide 50/50 cost share; OTAs must not duplicate existing DoD program efforts. OTA for prototypes: consistent with 10 U.S.C. 2371b; may be used for prototype projects relevant to mission effectiveness; no duplication of existing DoD efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funded Amount and Period of Performance variability
rubrics_metrics.description: The funded amount and period of performance of each selected proposal may vary depending on the technology area and the technical approach of the offeror.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No fixed award size or period; varies by topic and approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: White Paper Format Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: White Paper physical formatting: 8.5 x 11-inch paper, 1 inch margins, single-spaced, Times New Roman 12 point font, page limit 5 pages excluding cover page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover page is mandatory and FedConnect will not accept a white paper without the cover sheet. Titles should be descriptive of the work and not merely a copy of the announcement title.

rubrics_metrics.name: White Paper Submission technical requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic white papers (when required) must be Microsoft Word 2016 or PDF compatible format. There is an email size limit of 5MB per email. FedConnect is utilized for white paper submission where specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ONR/ONRG/MCWL have specified email addresses for electronic submission when applicable. Do not use FedConnect Messaging Center to submit white papers or questions. FedConnect registration steps (DUNS, SAM, SAM MPIN, create account) and support contact (support@fedconnect.net, 1-800-899-6665) are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: White Paper Content Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: White papers shall include: Cover Page (mandatory for ONR and ONRG), Technical Concept (description of technology innovation and technical risk areas), Future Naval Relevance, Operational Naval Concept (where applicable), Operational Utility Assessment Plan (where applicable), and Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover sheet must include Program Officer information (for ONR/ONRG the Program Officer/Science Director is required). Cover page templates provided at ONR web links. FedConnect will reject white papers without the cover sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full Proposal Requirements reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Full proposals must follow instructions in Appendix 1 for Grants/Cooperative Agreements/TIAs and Appendix 2 for Contracts and Other Transaction Agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See appendices for instrument-specific required content and forms; offerors should consult appropriate Appendix based on intended instrument type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Proprietary Statement of Work and proprietary marking legend
rubrics_metrics.description: For all proposals, a non-proprietary version of the Statement of Work (SOW) must be submitted. Do not put proprietary data or markings in or on the SOW. For data the offeror wishes to restrict, use the specified legend on the title page and mark each sheet to be restricted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legend text provided in BAA must be used. Each sheet with restricted data must bear the sheet-level legend. Proprietary markings and protections will be honored consistent with FAR Subpart 15.207 and applicable law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security Classification and classified proposal submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: White Papers and Proposals are expected to be unclassified; classified proposals are permitted but must be accompanied by an unclassified SOW. Classified proposals must be submitted to ONR’s Document Control Unit with specific outer/inner envelope addressing and classification markings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outer envelope: no classification marking and addressed to ONR Document Control Unit. Inner envelope: stamped with classification and addressed to the cognizant Technical POC. Follow the exact mailing instructions in the BAA for classified submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique Entity Identifier, DUNS and SAM registration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All offerors submitting proposals or applications must be registered in SAM prior to submission, provide a valid unique entity identifier in the application, and maintain active SAM registration with current information during any active award or proposal consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SAM may be accessed at https://www.sam.gov/SAM/. A Federal awarding agency may not make an award until an applicant has complied with UEI and SAM requirements; lack of compliance may render an applicant not qualified for award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission dates, announcement period and late proposal policy
rubrics_metrics.description: This announcement will remain open approximately one year from publication (proposals may be submitted at any time during this period). The Government reserves the right not to review proposals submitted after 30 September 2022, or after a successor BAA is issued, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors are urged to check ONR/SAM/Grants.gov for new BAA Calls. Late submissions may not be reviewed at the Government’s discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary Evaluation Criterion 1 — Scientific and technical merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall scientific and technical merits of the proposal and responsiveness to the topic: degree of innovation, soundness of technical concept, awareness of state of the art, understanding of problem scope, significance and originality of technical approach, effort needed to address the problem, and anticipated scientific impact within the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also consider (A) Offeror’s capabilities, related experience, facilities, techniques or unique combinations integral to achieving objectives; and (B) qualifications, capabilities and experience of proposed PI, team leader and key personnel critical to achieving objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary Evaluation Criterion 2 — Potential Naval relevance and contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential Naval relevance and contribution to ONR and Department of Navy mission; includes consideration of protection of intellectual property, controlled information, key personnel, and information about critical technologies relevant to national security and limiting undue influence (including foreign talent programs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration will be given to improper technology transfer, IP theft, cyber or human espionage, entities known to recruit foreign individuals to transfer knowledge, misleading information, concealed connections, or serious risks of improper transfer of non-public research. Offerors should be aware of NDAA-related restrictions and protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary Evaluation Criterion 3 — Availability of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of funds is a selection consideration (not applicable to white papers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria 1, 2 and 3 are equally important for selection decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost realism and reasonableness consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent appropriate, cost realism and reasonableness will be considered when selecting proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ONR reserves the right to request additional information and documentation after determining award instrument type and to remove offerors from consideration if agreement on terms/price cannot be reached or required information is not provided timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation process and selection steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals will not be evaluated against each other (not submitted to a common work statement); ONR intends to review proposals as they arrive; ultimate recommendation made by ONR scientific/technical community and forwarded to Contracts and Grant Awards Management for cost analysis and responsibility determinations. Selection recommendation does not guarantee award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain offerors may be required to demonstrate compliance with enhanced cybersecurity requirements prior to award. ONR may require additional documentation and may remove offerors who fail to reach agreement on award terms or fail to timely provide requested information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cybersecurity and enhanced security controls
rubrics_metrics.description: When warranted, performers may be required to implement enhanced cybersecurity controls to unclassified networks housing Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) in addition to DFARS 252.204-7012 requirements; certain efforts may require NIST SP 800-171 DoD assessment requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors are strongly encouraged to consult the cognizant Program Officer to determine whether enhanced cyber requirements will apply. Refer to Appendix 2, Federal Award Administration Information, for details on administrative and national policy requirements and cyber assessment clauses (e.g., 252.204-7012, 252.204-7019, 252.204-7020).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcontracting Plan requirement for certain contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposed contract awards exceeding $750,000, large businesses and non-profits (including educational institutions) must provide a Subcontracting Plan that contains all elements required by FAR 19.704 and FAR 52.219-9 and as supplemented by DFARS 252.219-7003.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small businesses are exempt. The Plan must be submitted as an attachment to the Proposal Checklist and will not be included in page count. Master/Individual/Comprehensive Plans must be attached if available. Plans will be reviewed for adequacy; failure to negotiate an acceptable Plan when required will render the apparent successful offeror ineligible for award. Offerors should propose realistic goals consistent with DoD subcontracting goals and include written justification if goals are below statutory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to small business participation and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR is committed to providing prime and subcontracting opportunities for small businesses (SDBs, WOSBs, HUBZone, VOSBs, SDVOSBs), HBCUs, MIs, and other socio-economic categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors unfamiliar with government contracting may use Procurement Technical Assistance Centers (PTACs), DAU Small Business COP, Dynamic Small Business Search, SAM contracting opportunities, Navy SBIR/STTR search, USAspending.gov, and other resources listed in the BAA to locate subcontracting partners and opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options evaluation method
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government will evaluate contract options for award purposes by adding the total cost for all options to the total cost for the basic requirement. Evaluation of options does not obligate the Government to exercise the options during performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government reserves the right to exercise options at time of award or later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational Conflicts of Interest (OCI) disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors who provide support services to ONR or are aware of circumstances that may result in an appearance of unfair competitive advantage must submit an OCI disclosure with their proposal containing: (i) name of entity supported, (ii) contract number creating OCI (or copy of document), (iii) concise description of actual/potential OCI including personal conflicts, (iv) Mitigation Plan, and (v) concluding certification statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to disclose actual/potential OCI will result in the offeror not being considered for award. The certification text is provided in the BAA and must be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCI Mitigation Plan minimum contents
rubrics_metrics.description: At a minimum, an OCI Mitigation Plan shall: (i) provide organizational charts showing elements creating the OCI; (ii) demonstrate how those elements will be isolated from resources performing under the BAA contract; (iii) show geographic/physical separation if applicable; (iv) describe personnel reassignment processes and restrictions; (v) describe controls including NDAs over future employment; (vi) describe OCI training offered/required; and (vii) provide evidence of facts/circumstances that mitigate OCI concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Contracting Officer will review OCI submissions and may require additional information; if OCI exists and cannot be mitigated, the Government may impose conditions, disqualify the offeror, award with mitigation, or seek a waiver. If accepted, the Mitigation Plan becomes part of the contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: TINA / Certified cost or pricing data requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All proposals submitted under this BAA that meet the Truth in Negotiations Act (TINA) threshold are subject to certified cost and pricing data. Offerors are required to execute the Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data as soon as practicable, but no later than five business days after the date of price agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost or pricing data submitted after price agreement will be reviewed after award to determine if certified data up to agreement was defective and whether Government is entitled to a price adjustment per FAR 52.215-10/11. The BAA references OUSD memorandum on eliminating inefficiencies associated with cost/pricing data submissions after price agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representations and disclosures re covered telecommunications and video surveillance equipment/services
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must comply with prohibitions in Section 889 of NDAA FY2019 regarding procurement/use of 'covered telecommunications equipment or services' (definitions provided). Offerors must represent whether they will/will not provide covered equipment/services and whether they do/do not use such equipment/services, and provide specified disclosures if answering affirmatively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors shall review SAM excluded parties list. If 'will' or 'does' is indicated, detailed disclosures about the equipment/service (manufacturer, model, use, PSC codes, etc.) must be provided as part of the offer in the format specified in the provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confucius Institute funding restriction (NDAA 2021 Sec.1062)
rubrics_metrics.description: Per NDAA 2021 Section 1062, beginning October 1, 2024, DoD may not fund institutions of higher education that host a Confucius Institute (as defined) other than amounts provided directly to students as education assistance, unless a waiver is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors should be aware this statutory restriction may affect eligibility for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model contracts/grants and precedence of clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: Model contracts and grants are provided as examples on ONR web links. In the event of any conflict between these examples and current FAR, DFARS, NMCARS, or ONR clauses, the current FAR/DFARS/NMCARS/ONR clauses will govern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors should consult the current regulations/clauses rather than relying solely on model documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection from disclosure and marking of proprietary information
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions will be protected from unauthorized disclosure in accordance with FAR Subpart 15.207, applicable law, and DoD/DoN regulations. Offerors are expected to appropriately mark each page of their submission that contains proprietary information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific legend language is provided for proposals that contain data the offeror does not want disclosed. Each sheet to be restricted must carry the sheet-level legend indicated in the BAA.
